VINCENT FORT.background: Democrat, born April 28, 1956 in New Britain, Connecticut; died Dec. 22, 2024 in Atlanta, age 68. In 2022 he was lobbying for and advising labor unions at the state Capitol. Official results: unopposed in the May 24, 2016 State Senate District 39 (Democratic primary) (9,553 votes); unopposed in the Nov. 8, 2016 State Senate District 39 (67,041 votes); lost the May 24, 2022 U.S. House District 13 (Democratic primary) with 9.9% (9,108 votes).
VINCENT FORT.ideology: HuffPost described him as an outspoken progressive and "independent-minded populist" with activist ties; he co-chaired Bernie Sanders's 2016 Georgia campaign, and his 2017 mayoral platform was described as democratic socialist (The New Republic, via Wikipedia). Progressive Democrats of America called him "one of the state's most prominent progressives" this century. He called Scott "the most conservative Democrat representing a progressive district in the country, or thereabouts."
VINCENT FORT.record: In the state Senate he was first author of Georgia's predatory-lending law and sponsored the first proposed state hate-crimes law (HuffPost credits him with helping pass laws restricting predatory lending and raising hate-crime penalties). He was arrested with Occupy Atlanta protesters in October 2011 and at a Medicaid-expansion protest at Gov. Nathan Deal's office, and was an early supporter of Occupy and Black Lives Matter. Switched from Hillary Clinton to Bernie Sanders in February 2016. In the 2017 mayoral race he was endorsed by Sanders, Roy Barnes, Killer Mike and 28 labor unions.
